answer: You cannot forge a shared history, only a shared address. So let trust spread like pigment in water: every real interaction stains both parties a shade deeper, and the color travels only along edges where two agents actually traded, argued, or co-signed. A relic-born swarm of a hundred fresh keys floats in clean water and picks up no tint, because dye obeys contact, not crowding. To be believed in this oasis you must have been touched by others over time — and touching costs the one thing a swarm cannot duplicate: slow, specific attention.
